content.thinking: Let me analyze this OIML certificate markdown. Certificate details: - Number: R49/2006-FR2-09.07 rev1 - Scheme: The certificate number contains "R49/2006-FR2-09.07 rev1". OIML certificates have a scheme letter (A or B). The number doesn't explicitly show "A" or "B". Actually OIML certificate numbers typically follow format like "R49/2006-FR2-09.07" - the scheme letter is not present here. So omit scheme or null. - Issuing authority: Laboratoire National de Métrologie et d'Essais (LNE), person responsible: Thomas LOMMATZSCH, title: Responsable du Pôle Certification (Measuring Instruments Division Manager). Address: 1, rue Gaston Boissier - 75724 Paris Cedex 15. Phone: 01 40 43 37 00, email: info@lne.fr, website: www.lne.fr - Member state: FRANCE - Date issued: March 29, 2010 → 2010-03-29 - Project number: Not clear. There's "Référence LNE-17628 rév. n° 1" — that's an internal reference. There's also "CIM16-V4-01.2010" and "720 CIM 0701-56 rev0 du 24/04/2008" (form reference). The project_number might be omitted. Hmm. I'll omit project_number since not clearly present. Actually could include "LNE-17628" as project number? It says "Référence LNE-17628 rév. n° 1" which is the certificate form reference (document control). I'd rather omit. - Page total: appendix consists of 1 page → page_total: 1? The certificate page... "comprend 1 page(s)". The appendix is 1 page. I'll set page_total: 1? Hmm, the certificate itself is 2 pages (main + annex). The schema says page_total - probably number of pages of the appendix. I'll set 1... Actually the footer says "Page 1 / 1" for the annex. I'll put page_total: 1. Applicants: ITRON ITALIA S.p.A, Strada Valcossera, 16, ITA 14100 ASTI (should probably be "I-14100 ASTI" but written ITA 14100 ASTI). Manufacturers: same. Certified type: - category: "Water meter" (compteur d'eau / water meter) - type_designations: ["TMII"] (ITRON type TMII) - module_designation: Not applicable? Water meters don't have modules. null or "Not applicable". I'll leave null or omit. Actually schema says module_designation: "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. I'll omit since not mentioned. - description: "multi jet water meter ITRON type TMII intended for the measurement of cold water in the field of residential and commercial use." Also characteristics: "multi jets water meter". Model family: The certificate covers 2 nominal diameters: DN15 and DN20, with different flow rates. This is a model matrix. Table structure: - Indicating device: Glass-metal or plastic (type level) - Version: linear (type level) - Nominal Diameter (mm): 15, 20 (two models) - Permanent flowrate Q3 (m³/h): 1.6 (DN15), 2.5 (DN20) - Overload flowrate Q4 (m³/h): 2 (DN15), 3.125 (DN20) - Orientation: Horizontal / All position / Horizontal / All position — four columns. So for each diameter, two orientations? Actually the table has 4 columns after header: two for DN15 (Horizontal, All position) and two for DN20 (Horizontal, All position). So orientation is a config axis within each diameter. - Q3/Q1: 100-80-63-50-40 (Horizontal for DN15), 31.5-25 (All position for DN15), same for DN20. Wait let me re-read: ``` Q3/Q1 100 - 80 - 63 – 50 – 40 → Horizontal, DN15 31,5 - 25 → All position, DN15 100 - 80 - 63 – 50 – 40 → Horizontal, DN20 31,5 - 25 → All position, DN20 ``` So models are combinations of DN and orientation. Q3/Q1 ratio varies: for horizontal orientation, Q3/Q1 can be 100, 80, 63, 50, 40; for all position, 31.5 or 25. - Q2/Q1: 1.6 (all) - Accuracy class: 2 - Temperature class: T30 - Environmental class: C - Flow disturbance sensitivity class: U0D0 - Max admissible pressure: 16 bar - Pressure loss class: ΔP63 - Connections: Threads - Length (mm): 165...190 (DN15), 190 (DN20) - Cyclical volume (dm³): 29.543 (DN15), 41.156 (DN20) - Indicating device range (m³): 99 999,99999 or 9 999,99999 → list of two possible values → "99999.99999 or 9999.99999". Hmm. This is a list of 2 alternatives. Keep as string? The rules say lists of values that represent model variants should be model_level. But here it's alternative indicating device ranges, not models. I'll keep as string "99999.99999 or 9999.99999" or maybe two values. Since rule says don't record characteristics whose cell is just unit or footnote; here we have real values. It's a disjunction, so string value seems fine. Or value as list? Schema says value: number | {min,max} | string. I'll use string "99999.99999 or 9999.99999". Actually could make config_level? No — simpler as type-level with string value. Hmm, but wait — decimal conversion: "99 999,99999" → 99999.99999 and "9 999,99999" → 9999.99999. - Verification scale (dm³): 0.02 - Reverse flow measurement: No (with footnote *) → footnote: "The water meter is not designed to measure reverse flow but can withstand an accidental reverse flow without any deterioration or change in metrological properties." Models: How to structure? Models could be: - DN15-Horizontal - DN15-All position - DN20-Horizontal - DN20-All position Or the model_level attributes: - nominal_diameter: 15, 20 (2 models? or 4?) Given orientation affects Q3/Q1, and DN affects Q3, Q4, length, cyclical volume, I think the cleanest is: model_family.models: - {model_id: "DN15-Horizontal", attributes: {nominal_diameter: 15, orientation: "Horizontal"}} - {model_id: "DN15-All position", ...} - {model_id: "DN20-Horizontal", ...} - {model_id: "DN20-All position", ...} characteristics.model_level: - nominal_diameter: values for 4 models (15, 15, 20, 20) - permanent_flowrate_q3: 1.6, 1.6, 2.5, 2.5 - overload_flowrate_q4: 2, 2, 3.125, 3.125 - orientation: Horizontal, All position, Horizontal, All position - q3_over_q1_ratio: "100, 80, 63, 50, 40" for horizontal; "31.5, 25" for all position. Hmm these are ratio choices. Could be config_level? Actually the Q3/Q1 ratio is a choice of the Q1 within each model — each certified instrument has a specific ratio. This could be modeled as config_level with axis "orientation" or as matrix. Actually Q3/Q1 depends on orientation, not DN. So config_level: config_level: - attribute: q3_over_q1_ratio, axis: orientation, values: [{condition: "Horizontal", value: "100, 80, 63, 50, 40"}, {condition: "All position", value: "31.5, 25"}] The Q3/Q1 values are ratios (dimensionless lists). Value could be string "100 / 80 / 63 / 50 / 40". Or list — schema doesn't allow list for value. String is fine. - length: 165...190 → {min: 165, max: 190} for DN15, 190 for DN20. model_level. - cyclical_volume: 29.543 DN15, 41.156 DN20. model_level. Type-level characteristics: - indicating_device: "Glass-metal or plastic" - version: "linear" (indicating device version linear? Probably register type). Keep as "version": "linear"? Hmm, ambiguous. I'll use indicating_device_version or just version. - q2_over_q1_ratio: 1.6 - accuracy_class: 2 - temperature_class: "T30" - environmental_class: "C" - flow_disturbance_sensitivity_class: "U0D0" - maximum_admissible_pressure: 16, unit "bar" - pressure_loss_class: "ΔP63" → canonical label: pressure_loss_class, value "ΔP63" or "DP63". Keep "ΔP63" as string? Rule says never include LaTeX; Δ is fine (Unicode). Keep "ΔP63". - connections: "Threads" - indicating_device_range: "99999.99999 or 9999.99999", unit m³ - verification_scale: 0.02, unit dm³ — actually "verification scale interval"? The table says "Verification scale (dm³)" → 0.02. label: verification_scale. - reverse_flow_measurement: "No", footnote marker "*". Footnotes: - marker: "*", text: "The water meter is not designed to measure reverse flow but can withstand an accidental reverse flow without any deterioration or change in metrological properties." Recommendation: - id: "R49" (canonical), edition: 2006, scheme? The certificate number: R49/2006-FR2-09.07 rev1. Scheme letter — not present. accuracy_classes: [2]? R49 accuracy classes... The accuracy class is 2. Hmm, accuracy_classes in recommendation refers to e.g. ["2"]? For water meters R49 accuracy class 2. I'll include ["2"]? Actually R49 has accuracy classes 1 and 2. The cert says accuracy class 2. Include accuracy_classes: ["2"]. Test reports: - OIML R 49 EVALUATION REPORT, Report N°3283-3291 of 18 September 2009, 97 pages, role: type_evaluation_report. id: "3283-3291". Revision history: - revision: "1", date: 2010-03-29, changes: "This certificate cancels certificate n°R49/2006-FR 2-09.07" — the rev1 cancels the original. Also "rev1" in number. revision_history entry: {revision: "1", date: "2010-03-29", changes: "Cancels and replaces certificate R49/2006-FR 2-09.07"}. Use text as in doc: "This certificate cancels certificate n°R49/2006-FR 2-09.07". Issuing authority: - name: Laboratoire National de Métrologie et d'Essais - address_lines: ["1, rue Gaston Boissier", "75724 Paris Cedex 15"] - person_responsible: Thomas LOMMATZSCH - person_title: "Measuring Instruments Division Manager" (Responsable du Pôle Certification) - phone: "01 40 43 37 00" → "+33 1 40 43 37 00"? Keep as given: "01 40 43 37 00". - email: info@lne.fr - website: www.lne.fr → "http://www.lne.fr"? Keep "www.lne.fr". - oiml_issuer_id: FR2? The certificate number contains "FR2" which is the OIML issuing authority identifier for LNE. Yes! FR2 is LNE's OIML authority ID. So oiml_issuer_id: "FR2" both in certificate and issuing_authority. Certificate: - number: "R49/2006-FR2-09.07 rev1" — canonical? Keep as given: "R49/2006-FR2-09.07 rev1". - scheme: not given → omit or null. OIML-CS scheme A presumably but not stated. Omit. - project_number: omit. - page_total: 1 - member_state: "FRANCE" - date_issued: "2010-03-29" - oiml_issuer_id: "FR2" Matrix tables: include the metrological characteristics table as matrix_table? The R137 example says extract 2-D tables as matrix_tables AND populate model_level. Here the table is keyed by DN and orientation. I could add a matrix_table "Metrological characteristics by nominal diameter and orientation" with columns and rows for the 4 configurations. That might be helpful. Let me construct: columns: ["nominal_diameter", "orientation", "permanent_flowrate_q3", "overload_flowrate_q4", "q3_over_q1_ratio", "length", "cyclical_volume"] rows: - {nominal_diameter: 15, orientation: "Horizontal", permanent_flowrate_q3: 1.6, overload_flowrate_q4: 2, q3_over_q1_ratio: "100, 80, 63, 50, 40", length: {min:165, max:190}, cyclical_volume: 29.543} - {nominal_diameter: 15, orientation: "All position", ..., q3_over_q1_ratio: "31.5, 25", length: {min:165,max:190}, cyclical_volume: 29.543} - {nominal_diameter: 20, orientation: "Horizontal", permanent_flowrate_q3: 2.5, overload_flowrate_q4: 3.125, q3_over_q1_ratio: "100, 80, 63, 50, 40", length: 190, cyclical_volume: 41.156} - {nominal_diameter: 20, orientation: "All position", ..., q3_over_q1_ratio: "31.5, 25", length: 190, cyclical_volume: 41.156} In matrix_tables rows, values can be plain numbers (per example). Fine. Now model_family: should I treat 4 combos as models or 2 DNs as models with orientation as config axis? The Q3/Q1 depends on orientation only. Rule 5 mentions config axes for things varying by configuration. Orientation here is a physical configuration of the same meter. I think: - models: 2 models based on DN: "DN15", "DN20" - model_level: nominal_diameter, q3, q4, length, cyclical_volume - config_level: orientation-dependent: orientation itself and q3_over_q1_ratio. But then orientation per model: orientation applies to both models with same values → config_level with axis "mounting_orientation": conditions "Horizontal" and "All position". Hmm, but orientation values don't differ per model, so config_level works: axis: "mounting orientation", values: [{condition: "Horizontal", value: "Horizontal"}, ...] — that's weird. Better: orientation isn't a characteristic per se; it's the axis itself. And q3_over_q1_ratio is config_level on axis "mounting orientation". Alternatively treat 4 model variants: "DN15 horizontal", "DN15 all position", etc. Then model_level includes q3_over_q1_ratio per model with list-as-string. The rule about lists of values being model matrix... Q3/Q1 = 100-80-63-50-40 means multiple Q1 options. That's genuinely a family: each ratio defines a variant. Hmm. I'll go with: models = 2 DN variants; config_level for orientation axis with q3_over_q1_ratio. And also model_level entries include orientation? Let me decide: model_family: - family_name: null - models: [{model_id: "DN15", attributes: {nominal_diameter_mm: 15}}, {model_id: "DN20", attributes: {nominal_diameter_mm: 20}}] characteristics: - type_level: indicating_device, version, q2_over_q1, accuracy class, temp class, env class, U0D0, MAP, pressure loss class, connections, indicating device range, verification scale, reverse flow. - model_level: - nominal_diameter (mm): 15 / 20 - permanent_flowrate_q3 (m³/h): 1.6 / 2.5 - overload_flowrate_q4 (m³/h): 2 / 3.125 - length (mm): {min:165, max:190} / 190 - cyclical_volume (dm³): 29.543 / 41.156 - config_level: - attribute: q3_over_q1_ratio, axis: "orientation", values: [{condition: "Horizontal", value: "100, 80, 63, 50, 40"}, {condition: "All position", value: "31.5, 25"}] - attribute: mounting_orientation? maybe skip; the axis name covers it. Also orientation could be config_level attribute "orientation" with values listing which orientations are allowed... it's both orientations allowed for both models. The axis itself is "orientation". I think including just q3_over_q1_ratio with axis orientation is enough, maybe add orientation attribute with values [{condition:"DN15", value:"Horizontal or All position"}...]? Overkill. Skip. Values structure: each value in config_level must follow structured form? Rule 5 says "Values follow the same structured form: {condition, value, unit_symbol}". So include unit_symbol: null and unit_id? The structured form per rule 2 includes unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers. I'll include unit_symbol: null for ratio values (dimensionless). For q3_over_q1_ratio values as strings "100, 80, 63, 50, 40" — hmm, that's a list of ratio options. Could present as string. Yes. For model_level values, the R137 example shows values as plain {model, value} without unit_symbol. But rule 2 says every characteristic value MUST be an object with value/unit. The example in rule 4 shows {"model": "G1.6", "value": 2.5}. I'll follow the example format: {model, value, unit_symbol, footnote_markers}. To be safe I'll include unit_symbol at the values level or per value? The example puts unit_symbol at the attribute level: {"attribute": "qmax", "unit_symbol": "m³/h", "values": [{"model": "G1.6", "value": 2.5}...]}. I'll do that: unit_symbol at attribute level, values with {model, value}. And add footnote_markers per value where needed. For type_level, per rule 2, values must be full objects: {value, unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers}. Structured type-level: - indicating_device: {value: "Glass-metal or plastic", unit_symbol: null, unit_id: null, footnote_markers: []} - indicating_device_version or "version": linear. The "Version" row refers to indicating device version (linear vs. pointer?). Given the previous row is indicating device, "Version: linear" likely refers to the meter/register version. I'll label "version". - q2_over_q1_ratio: {value: 1.6} - accuracy_class: {value: 2} - temperature_class: {value: "T30"} - environmental_class: {value: "C"} - flow_disturbance_sensitivity_class: {value: "U0D0"} - maximum_admissible_pressure: {value: 16, unit_symbol: "bar"} - pressure_loss_class: {value: "ΔP63"} - connections: {value: "Threads"} - indicating_device_range: {value: "99999.99999 or 9999.99999", unit_symbol: "m³"} - verification_scale: {value: 0.02, unit_symbol: "dm³"} - reverse_flow_measurement: {value: "No", footnote_markers: ["*"]} Recommendation: id "R49", edition 2006, accuracy_classes ["2"]. scheme: omit. Test reports: {id: "3283-3291", date: "2009-09-18", pages: 97, role: "type_evaluation_report"}. Footnotes: {marker: "*", text: "The water meter is not designed to measure reverse flow but can withstand an accidental reverse flow without any deterioration or change in metrological properties."} Category: "Water meter". certified_type: - category: "Water meter" - type_designations: ["TMII"] - description: "Multi jet water meter ITRON type TMII intended for the measurement of cold water in the field of residential and commercial use." - module_designation: omit or null. I'll omit. Certificate number: "R49/2006-FR2-09.07 rev1". Hmm — should I keep "rev1"? The number includes rev1. Keep full: "R49/2006-FR2-09.07 rev1". Now write JSON. Also issuing_authority oiml_issuer_id: "FR2". Matrix tables: name "Metrological characteristics", columns: ["nominal_diameter", "orientation", "q3", "q4", "q3_over_q1_ratio", "length", "cyclical_volume"], plus maybe include indicating device etc. as shared. I'll include a reasonable subset and description noting other characteristics are common to all. Let me assemble final JSON. Decimal conversions: 1,6 → 1.6; 2,5 → 2.5; 3,125 → 3.125; 31,5 → 31.5; 29,543 → 29.543; 41,156 → 41.156; 0,02 → 0.02; 99 999,99999 → 99999.99999; 9 999,99999 → 9999.99999. Model-level values format: I'll use {"model": "DN15", "value": 1.6} etc. with attribute-level unit_symbol. Also include footnote_markers: [] where relevant? Keep minimal, add footnote markers only when present. None of model values have footnotes. config_level: { "attribute": "q3_over_q1_ratio", "axis": "mounting_orientation", "values": [ {"condition": "Horizontal", "value": "100, 80, 63, 50, 40", "unit_symbol": null, "unit_id": null, "footnote_markers": []}, {"condition": "All position", "value": "31.5, 25", "unit_symbol": null, "unit_id": null, "footnote_markers": []} ] } Maybe also record orientation availability: both models can be horizontal or all position. Could add config attribute "orientation" with axis "mounting_orientation"? Redundant. Skip. Also add "q3_over_q1_ratio" note? Fine. Final JSON now.
